chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn 'Uqbah, from Abu Harun al-Makfuf, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and he said to me, 'Recite a poem for me.' So I recited, and he said, 'No, not the way you usually recite, but the way you eulogize him at his grave.' I said, so I recited: 'Pass by the grave of Husayn... and say to his pure bones...' He said, so when he cried, I stopped. He said, 'Pass (continue),' so I continued. He said, 'Add more, add more.' So I recited: 'O Maryam, arise and lament your master... and over Husayn, so be happy with your weeping.' He said, so he cried and the women became restless. He said, so when they calmed down, he said to me, 'O Abu Harun! Whoever recites a poem about Husayn (peace be upon him) and makes ten people cry, for him is Paradise.' Then he kept reducing one by one until he reached one, and said, 'Whoever recites a poem about Husayn and makes one person cry, for him is Paradise.' Then he said, 'Whoever remembers him and cries, for him is Paradise.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting poetry about Imam Husayn that makes others cry?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* underscores the Shia tradition of *rawda-khwani* (elegiac recitation) as a means of spiritual connection, where Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) validates the emotional impact of poetry by weeping himself. The Imam establishes a graduated reward system, culminating in Paradise for even a single person moved to tears, thereby elevating personal lamentation to a communal act of devotion. This highlights the theological significance of *al-mu'asara* (companionship) with the Ahl al-Bayt through emotional engagement with their suffering.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 5. Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan Al-Saffār, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā’īl, from Sāliḥ ibn ‘Uqbah, from Abī Hārūn Al-Makfūf, who said:

I went to Abī ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) and he asked me to recite a poem (about Ḥusain (a.s.)) for him. I started to recite a poem (without any intonation). So he (stopped me and) said, “No. Recite the way you usually recite (with intonation) and the way you recite eulogies by his grave.” I started to recite the poem (which begins with): “Pass by the grave of Ḥusain and say to his purified bones…” The Imam (a.s.) started to cry so I stopped. However, the Imam (a.s.) said to me, “Pass by (referring to the previous line of poetry, instructing me to continue).” After I finished reciting (this poem), Imam (a.s.) said, “Read more! Read more!” So I started reciting the following poem: O Maryam! Start the lamentation over your master, Ḥusain (a.s.), and shed abundant tears over him. When I read this verse, the Imam (a.s.) cried and the women (in his house) also cried and became restless. After the women calmed down, the Imam (a.s.) said to me: O Abā Hārūn! Anyone who recites a poem about Ḥusain (a.s.) and makes ten people cry will be rewarded with Paradise. Then he kept reducing the number from ten (people) one by one until he reached one (person) and said: Anyone who recites a poem about Ḥusain (a.s.) and makes one person cry will be rewarded with Paradise. He (the Imam (a.s.)) added, “Anyone who remembers Ḥusain (a.s.) and cries will be rewarded with Paradise.”
